text:
maya: Heads-up — acme-prod dedicated pool eu-west-1 seeing p95 token latency spikes + 429s for tenant 'brightbeam' starting ~08:40 UTC. Likely noisy neighbor on node-3a. Anyone oncall?

devon: oncall here, investigating. Can you paste pool/node IDs + model + MIG config?

maya: Pool: ded-eu2-03, node: node-3a, tenant: brightbeam-007, model: llm-13b-q4_0, MIG: 3g. Observed p95 -> 800ms from ~120ms baseline; 429 spike correlated with SM saturation.

ops-bot: alert: GPU anomaly detected on node-3a — SM util spike (95%), memory util ~60% on GPU0, other GPUs idle.

lin: can you grab nvtop + a quick nsys snapshot? also check dmesg for any PCIe/ECC warnings — want to rule out HW.

maya: attaching quick snippet from node-3a: ```
nvtop --pid 1234: MIG slice 0 high sm, process: /usr/bin/infer_worker --tenant=brightbeam-007
nvidia-smi dmon: GPU0 sm 96% (sampl), GPU1-3 sm <10%
```

devon: looks like a co-tenant is running heavy kernels on that MIG slice. Autoscaler should react — what's the autoscale config for that pool? any recent scale events?

sara: ded-eu2-03 autoscale: min=2 max=6 target_util=70%, burst disabled. Cluster events show node count stable at 3 for last 45m, no scale triggers during the spike window.

oncall: suspect noisy neighbor due to MIG fragmentation — some tenants pinned to 1g/3g mixes. Large-kernel loads can thrash L3/cache and raise latency for adjacent slices. Can we repro by running a stress job?

devon: repro plan: on repro node run SM-heavy workload and a small inference client. Example command: ```kubectl exec -it repro-pod -- bash -c 'python stress_sm.py --batch 64 --seq_len 1024'``` then curl the inference endpoint in a tight loop to measure p95 and 429s.

maya: I ran that on node-3a in staging — when stress starts, p95 climbs and after ~30s requests start getting 429s as the request queue backlogs. No nvlink/dmesg errors; seems interference not HW fault.

lin: recommended immediate mitigations: 1) migrate brightbeam off node-3a to a different node 2) temporarily bump autoscale max or enable burst policy so new nodes can absorb load 3) throttle the noisy co-tenant if we can identify it.

sara: initiating migration: `/run move_tenant --tenant brightbeam-007 --to ded-eu2-05` — ETA ~2m. Notifying scheduler and billing not to count a migration event.

ops-bot: task started: tenant migration brightbeam-007 -> ded-eu2-05 (task id: mig-1977654321-1).

maya: after migration p95 back ~130ms and 429s stopped. nvtop now shows GPU0 SM util down to 18%, node-3a GPU0 returns to idle. Observed transient queue clear.

devon: follow-up items: investigate autoscaler hysteresis around per-MIG hot spots, add metric/alert for per-slice L3 thrash and per-MIG sm skew, consider enabling burst for this pool. @lin @sara please file infra ticket and timeline.

lin: noted — I'll open ticket with repro steps, nvtop/nsys snippet, and a graph of per-MIG SM util + tail latency.

sara: added to infra board and pinged account team to inform acme. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks all — leaving logs + traces in support case #S-19776 for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
